numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The decomposition should finish. For the 2x2 test A=[[a, k*a],[b, k*b]] the expected results are A.rank()==1, Q.cols==A.rank(), and (Q*R - A) simplifies to zeros(2,2).

category_specific_evidence: Test test_QR_symbolic_dependent_columns uses a 2x2 symbolic matrix A=[[a, k*a],[b, k*b]] with real symbols a, b, k, where columns are dependent and rank is 1; asserts A.rank()==1, Q.cols==A.rank(), no NaN in Q.H*Q after simplify, and (Q*R - A) simplifies to zeros(2,2).

Patch changes _QRdecomposition_optional so that a column is skipped when its zero-ness is undetermined (z is None) and dps(dot(Q[:,j],Q[:,j])) equals 0, instead of dividing by a norm that may be zero.

Reviewer comment states that using .equals to check zero on large symbolic expressions is not a good approach and that Matrix.QRdecomposition should use the DomainMatrix implementation for symbolic matrices; the patch is described as a reasonable improvement only to the _QRdecomposition_optional function.
Commit and release note describe the fix as handling rank of matrices with symbols in QR decomposition.

Behaviour depends on symbolic simplification and .equals, so results may be sensitive to simplification; no numeric tolerance is specified.
Reviewer notes the fix covers only _QRdecomposition_optional, not Matrix.QRdecomposition, so reproduction should target the intended method carefully.
